cms.hero.desc: A custom content management system, built from scratch to power this blog — designed from day one to be reused on other sites.
cms.overview.heading: What it is and why
cms.overview.p1: Instead of relying on a third-party CMS to publish to the blog, I built my own: an API that stores posts in Firestore, and a separate admin panel to create, edit, schedule and manage everything without touching code or hand-crafting requests.
cms.overview.p2: The goal from the start wasn't just to solve this once — it was to build something genuinely reusable. Every site-specific setting (target repository, image bucket, allow-listed emails) lives in environment variables, not in the code. Reusing this CMS for another site is a matter of configuration, not a rewrite.
cms.architecture.heading: Architecture
cms.architecture.subtitle: Two repositories, each with a clear responsibility.
cms.architecture.backend.title: Backend — cms
cms.architecture.backend.desc: A Node.js/Express REST API, deployed as a Cloud Function (2nd gen) on Firebase. Stores posts in Firestore and images in Firebase Storage.
cms.architecture.backend.item1: Dual authentication: an API key for scripts, or a Firebase Auth token checked against an allow-list of emails
cms.architecture.backend.item2: Scheduled publishing, checked automatically every 5 minutes
cms.architecture.backend.item3: Triggers the site rebuild (GitHub Actions) whenever a post is published
cms.architecture.backend.item4: Image uploads with type and size validation
cms.architecture.frontend.title: Admin panel — cms-admin
cms.architecture.frontend.desc: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript — no framework, no build step. Talks directly to the backend's API and to Firebase Authentication.
cms.architecture.frontend.item1: Google sign-in, restricted to an allow-list of emails
cms.architecture.frontend.item2: Single session per device: signing in on one signs the others out
cms.architecture.frontend.item3: Session automatically ends after 15 minutes of inactivity
cms.architecture.frontend.item4: Post drafts are autosaved and recoverable on any device
cms.features.heading: Key features
cms.features.preview.title: Real-time preview
cms.features.preview.desc: Split screen: the editor on one side, a live preview on the other, updated on every change.
cms.features.schedule.title: Post scheduling
cms.features.schedule.desc: Set a date and the post publishes itself — no need to be online at the time.
cms.features.images.title: Image library
cms.features.images.desc: Upload, reuse and delete images — with a warning when an image is still in use in some post.
cms.features.search.title: Search and overview
cms.features.search.desc: A panel with totals by status, and filters by title, tag, status and publish date.
cms.features.security.title: Session security
cms.features.security.desc: Single session per device, plus automatic sign-out after inactivity.
cms.features.recovery.title: Draft recovery
cms.features.recovery.desc: Work in progress is autosaved, even if the session gets interrupted.
cms.reuse.heading: How to reuse it on another site
cms.reuse.subtitle: None of this requires changing code — just configuring it.
cms.reuse.step1: Clone both repositories (cms and cms-admin) and create a new Firebase project with Firestore, Storage and Authentication (Google Sign-In) enabled.
cms.reuse.step2: Configure the backend's secrets: an API key, the allow-list of emails with write access, and (optionally) the target repository and the image bucket.
cms.reuse.step3: Point the admin panel's Firebase config at your new project, and deploy the backend and the panel.
cms.reuse.step4: Integrate your site with the CMS's REST API (a simple GET /posts) to list and render published posts.
cms.links.heading: See the code, or the result live
cms.links.desc: The code for both repositories is public. And the blog you're reading right now is this CMS's own result, in production.
